_about: Machine-readable expectations for the multi-resume diagnostic eval suite. All resumes are SYNTHETIC. These are coarse product-level expectations, NOT a pass/fail accuracy benchmark. 'primary_domains'/'secondary_domains' are the domain tokens fed to the existing ranking algorithm per persona (they drive domain-aware JD selection AND the domain_alignment fit cap); the *_role_families fields are used only to label eval results. See docs/EVAL_SUITE.md.
_domain_note: domain_alignment maps a JD role_family to domain tokens via ROLE_FAMILY_TO_DOMAINS, then compares against primary/secondary. Because 'fullstack' expands to {fullstack, frontend, backend, web}, a fullstack JD can resolve to 'strong' (not 'adjacent') whenever the persona's primary domain is frontend or backend. That is acceptable: the eval treats strong and adjacent both as non-mismatch.

backend_platform.notes: Backend/server/platform roles should rank above frontend-only and AI/security roles. A fullstack JD may resolve to strong (it subsumes backend). ML/data/frontend should be weak; marketing/design/product must rank last.

junior_frontend.notes: Junior/new-grad frontend. Frontend (and frontend-heavy fullstack) should rank top. Senior frontend roles requiring 3-5y stay frontend-domain (strong) but should earn a LOWER fit_level due to experience_level prerequisite gaps — this tests experience capping, not domain. Backend/infra/android weak; marketing/design/product last.

ai_ml_application.notes: AI/ML application engineer. AI/ML/LLM/RAG roles should rank top; data and backend-AI-platform adjacent. Frontend/android/security weak; marketing/design/product last. Note: live JD pools may contain few ml_ai roles — invariants that need an ml_ai JD are reported 'n/a' if none was selected.

devops_infra_security.notes: DevOps/infra/platform with security-adjacent exposure. Infra/SRE/AIOps/cloud roles should rank top; security detection/response and backend platform adjacent. Frontend/ml/data weak; marketing/design/product last.
